column12: Judgement on the comparator. Ultomiris is the closest marketed product in the same disease and mechanism: a C5 inhibitor labelled for adults with AChR antibody-positive gMG, the population cemdisiran was filed for. Zilbrysq, the other C5 in gMG and also subcutaneous, has no row in the book's CMS table. Case against: Ultomiris's Medicare spend mixes PNH, aHUS, NMOSD and gMG patients, and a per-beneficiary figure includes partial years. Vyvgart, the gMG volume leader and the anchor of the book's nipocalimab seed, reads $231,053 per Part B beneficiary (30% lower), and Soliris biosimilars (Bkemv is in the book) now compete on C5 price. Case for higher: Soliris reads $352,952 (Part B 2024), and Zilbrysq's US list price is about $1,164 per daily 23 mg syringe (UCB US pricing page, ucb-usa.com/Sustainability/Affordability/ZILBRYSQ-Pricing-Info, as quoted in a search result and not opened), roughly $425,000 a year at WAC. No price for cemdisiran has been published

column12: Judgement: not the book's anti-FcRn figure (0.5, nipocalimab seed), because a C5 inhibitor is continuous maintenance therapy while efgartigimod is often given in cycles with drug holidays; zilucoplan is the closest analogue (subcutaneous C5, recent entrant against FcRn alternatives). Other C5 evidence brackets it: ravulizumab, Italian early access, 3 of 24 stopped over a median 26 weeks (Rossini et al., J Neurol 2025, PMID 40366475), about 0.23 a year; eculizumab, Japan MG registry, 13 of 36 did not continue over a mean 35 months of treatment (Tokuyasu et al., Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2024, PMID 38572524), about 0.14 a year. Case for higher: only 30 of the 48 French patients reached six months, so 7 of 48 understates the six-month hazard, and early-access cohorts are motivated, refractory patients. In NIMBLE no cemdisiran patient stopped for an adverse event over 24 weeks, but trial retention is not real-world persistence

Two filters for the label population, adults with generalised MG who are AChR antibody-positive (the NDA population; NIMBLE also enrolled LRP4-positive patients, Lancet 2026, PMID 42030965). (1) Generalised, not ocular-only: a Mayo Clinic population-based study found 51% of patients presented with ocular onset and 55% of these generalised (as cited in Dresser L et al., J Clin Med 2021;10(11):2235, doi:10.3390/jcm10112235, section 3.1.2, the review the book's nipocalimab seed uses), so 1 - 0.51 x 0.45 = 0.7705 are generalised. (2) AChR antibody-positive within gMG: 'Eighty-five percent of people with gMG are AChR antibody-positive' (AstraZeneca 6-K 0001654954-26-008478, 2026-09-21, Klygefa CHMP release). 0.7705 x 0.85 = 0.6549, or 54,172 US adults
column12: Cross-check from Dresser alone: AChR antibodies in about 80% of all MG and in over half of ocular MG, so AChR-positive gMG is at most 0.80 - 0.2295 x 0.5 = 0.685 of all MG, consistent. Judgement: no severity filter. NIMBLE required MG-ADL of 6 or more, but the C5 labels in gMG (Ultomiris, Zilbrysq, and Klygefa's CHMP wording 'adults who are anti-AChR antibody-positive') carry no severity threshold. Case against: payers may restrict to more severe or refractory patients. The peak penetration is solved on this same pool, so the choice does not inflate uptake. LRP4-positive patients are left out (Lrp4 antibodies in 2-50% of double-seronegative MG, Dresser 2021). This differs from the nipocalimab seed's 0.87 because that label also covers MuSK-positive patients; that seed applies no ocular filter

column11: Solved from Vyvgart, the first anti-FcRn in gMG: 'We grew our global commercial footprint in gMG to reach more than 10,000 patients' in 2024 (argenx FY2024 20-F, 0001697862-25-000024). Through the engine with Vyvgart's own inputs: pool 82,715 x 0.6549 = 54,172 US, scaled by Vyvgart's 2024 ex-US multiple 0.1529 ((89.4 + 39.2 + 161.4) / 1,895.9, argenx FY2025 20-F 0001697862-26-000032) to 62,457; the book's Vyvgart curve (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0, first year 2022) and discontinuation 0.5 (nipocalimab seed) put the 2024 stock at 0.7426 x peak x 62,457, so 10,000 patients gives a Vyvgart peak of 0.2156. Cemdisiran = 0.25 x 0.2156 x (0.2704 / 0.5) = 0.02915
column12: Judgement: a multiple of 0.25 on Vyvgart's plateau treated share (peak / discontinuation, 43.1% of the AChR-positive gMG pool), which gives cemdisiran a plateau of 10.8%, about 5,800 US patients. The discontinuation ratio converts the stock share into a starts share, since cemdisiran's persistence is set higher than Vyvgart's. Check: the Vyvgart peak implies 13,581 patients in 2025 against argenx's 'more than 19,000 patients across three indications (gMG, CIDP, and ITP)' (FY2025 20-F). This build gives about $1.57bn of revenue in 2034 before the royalty, against GlobalData's forecast of about $1.9bn for pozelimab + cemdisiran in the 7MM by 2034 (Clinical Trials Arena, clinicaltrialsarena.com/analyst-comment/phase-iii-regeneron-pozelimab-cemdisiran-mg/, as summarised in a search result and not opened), which a multiple near 0.30 would match. Case for higher: dosing every 12 weeks is the least frequent in gMG; Regeneron claims the best MG-ADL improvement among C5 inhibitors in Phase 3 (8-K 0001104659-26-002691; cross-trial: 2.3 points against 1.6 for gefurulimab in PREVAIL, AstraZeneca 6-K 0001654954-26-008478). Case for lower: cemdisiran enters as the fourth or fifth C5 option (Soliris and its biosimilars, Ultomiris, Zilbrysq, gefurulimab under US review) behind three anti-FcRns (Vyvgart, Rystiggo, Imaavy), with partial complement inhibition on monotherapy (about 74% on average, against about 99% for the combination, as reported by NeurologyLive and quoted in a search result); 'reach more than 10,000 patients' may count patients ever treated, which would overstate Vyvgart's peak
